summary:
Parallax is an open observatory for the changing infrared sky. Stars aren't fixed in place: nearby ones drift across the sky year by year. Parallax lets anyone watch that happen in real NASA SPHEREx infrared images and measure it, with honest uncertainties and no astronomy background needed

How it works: PARALLAX uses real SPHEREx Level 2 images from NASA/IPAC IRSA (DR1 and QR3), with saved copies so the demo works offline. It reads each image's own calibration for wavelength and flags, measures from the archive pixel values rather than the display picture, and explains every view in plain language.
details: PARALLAX is a free, interactive web application that makes NASA's SPHEREx infrared observations accessible to everyone. Using real data from NASA/IPAC's archive, users can explore the sky, watch how stars move over time, and investigate changes through an interactive flipbook and sky viewer. The app aligns observations, visualizes different infrared wavelengths, and measures stellar motion while accounting for uncertainty and potential imaging artifacts. For example, PARALLAX measured Barnard's Star moving at 9.84 ± 0.36 arcseconds per year using 58 observations, close to its known motion of approximately 10.4. Built with TypeScript, React, and Python, the application combines scientific analysis with an approachable, retro-inspired interface that helps beginners understand what they're seeing without limiting more advanced exploration. Our goal is to make astronomical data easier to explore while showing how scientists distinguish genuine discoveries from measurement errors. PARALLAX runs entirely on free infrastructure, uses publicly available NASA data, and allows anyone with a browser to explore the changing infrared sky.
